# Phase 3 results: own-price elasticity (generated by scripts/30_phase3_elasticity.py)

Specification per product: `ln(units) ~ ln(shelf price) + feature + display + store FE + week-of-year FE`, OLS, standard errors clustered by store. Elasticity = coefficient on ln(price).

- 55 products estimated. Median elasticity **-1.78**, IQR -2.52 to -0.96.
- 55 of 55 are negative; 40 fall in the textbook -1 to -4 band.
- Without the feature/display controls the median elasticity is **-2.13**: the price variable then absorbs display and circular support, overstating price sensitivity.
- Mean effect of a feature on ln(units) holding price fixed: +0.25 (x1.29); of a display: +0.33 (x1.39).

## Assumption stated honestly

Price is treated as exogenous conditional on store, seasonality and promo-support controls. It is not fully: retailers cut price when they expect demand to respond, and base-price changes may follow cost changes that also shift demand. With more data I would instrument shelf price with wholesale-cost shocks or use competitor pricing as a control. Treat these as reduced-form 'promotional' elasticities, which is what a trade-promotion planner needs anyway.
